story.vex: History repeats. So will I. (Commander Vex, Planet Doom)
story.victory: DOOM ATTACK REPELLED, in spirit: the crew now understands why every old layer still matters. Astro: "We didn't remove a single lock. We just kept adding more."

files.C:\\Citadel\\README.txt:
ORDERS FROM ASTRO
=================
Volt left four archive notes, one per era of Citadel security. Read them in order, oldest first, then classify each control by its era.

1. type archive\era-1.txt, era-2.txt, era-3.txt, era-4.txt
2. classify each control: lock-door era1, admin-password era2, firewall era3, verify-every-request era4
files.C:\\Citadel\\archive\\era-1.txt:
ERA 1 — PHYSICAL
Codexia's founding console had one control: a locked door. No network, no password, just a guard on watch.
files.C:\\Citadel\\archive\\era-2.txt:
ERA 2 — SINGLE MACHINE
The first computer arrived. One shared admin password kept out anyone without it. The door still stayed locked too.
files.C:\\Citadel\\archive\\era-3.txt:
ERA 3 — NETWORKED
Terminals were wired together. Rivet built the first firewall, because now an attack could arrive over the wire, not just through the door.
files.C:\\Citadel\\archive\\era-4.txt:
ERA 4 — ZERO TRUST (today)
The Citadel now talks to three allied fleets. Every request is verified, whether it claims to come from inside or outside. Nothing from Eras 1-3 was removed.

steps.title: Volt's Archive: read the four eras
steps.body: Volt: "Oldest first. Notice what stays." Read all four era files in `archive\`.

steps.title: Sort each control into its era
steps.body: Rivet: "Four controls, four eras. Tag each one." `classify lock-door era1`, `classify admin-password era2`, `classify firewall era3`, `classify verify-every-request era4`.
